## Summary
This postmortem covers a minor service degradation in notification-service that began at 11:46 UTC on June 27, 2026 and affected approximately 36% of requests during the incident window.

## Root Cause
A deploy to notification-service at 11:46 UTC introduced a change to the caching layer. The change passed CI but the test suite did not reproduce the production traffic shape, and the regression only became visible once real user traffic hit the new code path.

## Detection & Response
The incident was detected by automated alerting 5 minutes after onset, when p99 latency crossed its configured threshold. On-call acknowledged within 8 minutes and began triage immediately, correlating the alert storm across 3 affected services before identifying notification-service as the origin.

## Resolution
The team mitigated impact by reverting the offending change and redeploying the previous version, which brought error rates back to baseline within 12 minutes of the mitigation being applied. Full resolution, including validation that downstream services had recovered, was confirmed 23 minutes after the incident began.

## Contributing Factors
- feature flag was enabled for 100% of traffic instead of a gradual ramp
- load test suite did not cover the changed code path

## Preventive Action
Extend the canary stage to a minimum of 30 minutes with automated error-budget gating.
